EF Core docs: with a relational database, data access is performed through a context object (DbContext) representing a session with the database, backed by a model of entity classes; querying returns entity-class instances, retrieved via LINQ.

claims.text: EF Core docs, verbatim: "By convention, when using a relational database, entity properties are mapped to table columns having the same name as the property." A different column name needs explicit Fluent API or attribute configuration.
Product (DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs) is a plain class with exactly three properties (Id, Name, PriceVnd), no data-access attributes, no base class — nothing in the class itself refers to a database.

DonHangDbContext.OnModelCreating maps Product with e.ToTable("products") and one e.Property(p => p.X).HasColumnName("x") call per property (Id→id, Name→name, PriceVnd→price_vnd), matching EF Core's own documented Fluent API shape for a non-default column name.
